pr_title: drivers: interrupt_controller: esp32c6: reserve IRQ 1 for WiFi
pr_body:
IRQ 1 is reserved for WiFi in ESP-IDF, which is used as the basis for the Espressif HAL in Zephyr.

If IRQ 1 is used by Zephyr and too many other peripherals (e.g. multiple UARTs) are enabled, WiFi stops working.

Marking IRQ 1 as "not available" seems to fix the issue.

Fixes #82874
pr_comments:
Here is the link to the relevant code in ESP-IDF: https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/master/components/esp_hw_support/port/esp32c6/esp_cpu_intr.c

We are not totally sure if IRQ 1 is actually used for WiFi in Zephyr as well. The WiFi driver does not use the Zephyr interrupt controller, but allocates its ISRs independently (inside the HAL repo). So we assumed it could be the same IRQ as used by ESP-IDF.

Espressif experts, please double-check if this is correct.
@martinjaeger Hey, great you fixed this. BTW, I have been updating C3/C6 interrupt controller to improve it. It means this change might go away in a couple of days. Anyway, LGTM.

> Here is the link to the relevant code in ESP-IDF: https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/master/components/esp_hw_support/port/esp32c6/esp_cpu_intr.c
> 
> We are not totally sure if IRQ 1 is actually used for WiFi in Zephyr as well. The WiFi driver does not use the Zephyr interrupt controller, but allocates its ISRs independently (inside the HAL repo). So we assumed it could be the same IRQ as used by ESP-IDF.
> 
> Espressif experts, please double-check if this is correct.

Exactly, that is part of the changes I've been adding to C3/C6 (riscv) interrupt allocator.

issue_context.title: WiFi doesn't seem to work on ESP32-C6
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The WiFi Support added in #81078 doesn't seem to work. Running `wifi scan` on the WiFi shell on a XIAO ESP32-C6 never outputs anything.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. `west build -b xiao_esp32c6 samples/net/wifi/shell -p`
2. `west flash`
3. `picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyACM0 --lower-dtr`
4. Run `wifi scan`

Nothing happens.

Also the `connect` commands don't work.

**Expected behavior**

Output of the WiFi scan.

**Impact**

Showstopper for our project.

**Logs and console output**

```
...
I (154) boot: Jumping to the main image...
I (178) heap_runtime: ESP heap runtime init at 0x4083bcb0 size 258 kB.

[00:00:00.022,000] <err> entropy: Error enabling TRNG clock
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v4.0.0-1883-g6dafb5f4a9cb ***
uart:~$ 
uart:~$ wifi scan
Scan requested
uart:~$ 
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Manjaro Linux
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA: 6dafb5f4a9cbd7043989f986d1f5963c264d413e
comments: @martinjaeger I figured that Wi-Fi is working, but if fails when `usb_serial` is `okay`. I am checking the root cause.

Thanks for the initial investigation. I tried again with `usb_serial` disabled and `wifi scan` does indeed work. However, if I run `wifi connect`, it doesn't get assigned an IP and `wifi status` always prints `SCANNING`. I used the same commands which are working fine on an ESP32C3 board.
Bump CONFIG_NET_MGMT_EVENT_QUEUE_SIZE from 16 to 24. The default 16 causes problems with events getting propagated to the proper place.
Ok, got it to work with disabled `usb_serial` on latest main (commit d27e4dc463890ea2adcfcd78212006b04edaa21a).
FWIW, it's not only the `usb_serial` is causing trouble. WiFi also stops working if you enable `uart1` (which we need in our application for a Modbus interface). This is really weird...

review_comments:
ESP32-xtensa's interrupt allocator uses (as done in esp-idf) IRQ 6 to control disabled interrupts. So it would be good to change this to 
```c
    [5] = {IRQ_FREE, IRQ_FREE},
    [6 ... 7] = {IRQ_NA, IRQ_NA},
```
However, as said, ESP32-risc's implementation (in Zephyr) does not use this yet. I shall update in a another PR. LGTM.
Ok. Let's update that as soon as it's used for Zephyr. Maybe together with your upcoming interrupt controller update.
